title: Chicken Soup
description: A comforting chicken soup with vegetables, noodles, and fresh parsley.

title: Beef and Carrot Stew
description: Slow-simmered beef and carrots in a savory red-wine broth.
notes: For best texture, keep the stew at a quiet simmer rather than a rolling boil.
body:
Pat @beef chuck{700%g} dry and season with @salt{1%tsp} and @black pepper{0.5%tsp}. Brown in batches in a heavy pot with @olive oil{15%ml}, then set aside. Soften @onion{1} and @carrot{3} in the pot; stir in @garlic clove{2} and @tomato paste{20%g}.

Stir in @plain flour{15%g}, then gradually add @red wine{250%ml} and @beef stock{500%ml}, scraping the pot. Return the beef with @bay leaf{1} and @thyme{2%sprig}. Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 hours; add a splash of water if needed. Remove the herbs and adjust seasoning.

title: Spinach and Ricotta Lasagne
description: A layered pasta bake with spinach, ricotta, tomato sauce and browned mozzarella.
notes: Use oven-ready sheets only if their package directions match the sauce amount.
body:
Heat @olive oil{15%ml} in a pan and soften @onion{1}. Add @garlic clove{2}, @crushed tomato{800%g}, @dried oregano{1%tsp}, @salt{1%tsp} and @black pepper{0.5%tsp}; simmer 20 minutes. Wilt @spinach{300%g}, cool, squeeze dry and chop. Mix it with @ricotta{400%g}, @egg{1} and half of @parmesan{50%g}.

Heat oven to 190°C conventional (170°C fan). Spread a little tomato sauce in a baking dish. Layer @lasagne sheet{250%g}, the ricotta mixture and sauce, finishing with sauce; cover with @mozzarella{150%g} and the remaining parmesan. Bake 35–40 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: No-Knead Country Bread
description: A crusty round loaf with an open, chewy crumb made with a long room-temperature rise.
notes: Dough hydration is high; use wet hands for folds. Oven temperatures are suggestions for a home oven.
body:
Mix @bread flour{500%g}, @water{375%ml}, @instant yeast{1%g} and @salt{10%g} until no dry flour remains. Cover and rest 30 minutes. With a damp hand, pull an edge of dough up and fold it over; rotate and repeat on all four sides. Cover and leave at room temperature until roughly doubled, about 8–12 hours.

Turn onto a lightly floured surface, shape into a tight round and rest seam-side down under a towel for 30 minutes. Meanwhile heat a lidded Dutch oven at 230°C conventional (210°C fan) for 30 minutes. Carefully transfer dough seam-side up into the hot pot, cover and bake 30 minutes; uncover and bake 15–20 minutes until deep golden. The centre should reach about 96°C. Cool fully on a rack before slicing.

title: Chickpea, Cucumber and Feta Salad
description: A crisp, lemony salad of chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, herbs and salty feta.
body: Whisk @lemon juice{30%ml} with @extra-virgin olive oil{30%ml}, @salt{0.5%tsp} and @black pepper{0.25%tsp}. Toss @chickpea{2%can}, drained and rinsed, with @cucumber{1}, @cherry tomato{200%g}, @red onion{0.5} and @parsley{15%g}; coat with the dressing. Fold in @feta{100%g} gently. Taste and adjust the seasoning; serve promptly or chill briefly.

title: Chicken Piccata with Lemon-Caper Sauce
description: Golden chicken cutlets finished in a bright pan sauce of lemon, capers and butter.
notes: Chicken cutlets should reach 74°C at the thickest point.
body:
Season @chicken breast{600%g}, sliced horizontally into 4 cutlets, with @salt{0.75%tsp} and @black pepper{0.25%tsp}; dredge lightly in @plain flour{40%g}. Heat @olive oil{30%ml} and half of @butter{40%g} in a wide pan. Cook the chicken in batches until golden and 74°C at the thickest point; transfer to a plate.

Add @chicken stock{150%ml}, @lemon juice{30%ml} and @capers{25%g}, drained, to the pan, scraping up browned bits. Simmer until slightly reduced. Whisk in the remaining butter off the heat, return chicken and juices to the pan, and turn to coat. Scatter @parsley{10%g} over the sauce and serve.

title: Mushroom and Barley Risotto
description: Pearl barley cooked until tender in mushroom stock, finished with parmesan.
notes: Pearl barley takes longer than rice; add hot stock gradually and taste for tenderness.
body:
Warm @olive oil{20%ml} and @butter{20%g} in a broad pan. Brown @mixed mushroom{300%g} in batches; reserve. Soften @onion{1}, add @garlic clove{2} briefly, then stir in @pearl barley{250%g} until glossy. Pour in @white wine{100%ml} and stir until mostly absorbed.

Add hot @vegetable stock{900%ml} one ladle at a time, stirring often and allowing each addition to absorb before adding more. Continue until barley is tender with a slight bite, 35–45 minutes; add hot water if stock runs short. Fold in the mushrooms and @parmesan{50%g}, season with @salt{0.5%tsp} and @black pepper{0.25%tsp}, and rest covered for 2 minutes.

title: Roasted Salmon with Mustard-Dill Cream
description: Oven-roasted salmon served with a cool mustard, dill and yoghurt sauce.
notes: For food safety, cook salmon to 63°C in the thickest part; adjust for local guidance and preference.
body:
Heat oven to 200°C conventional (180°C fan). Set @salmon fillet{600%g}, skin-side down and divided into 4 portions, on a lined tray; brush with @olive oil{10%ml} and season with @salt{0.75%tsp} and @black pepper{0.25%tsp}. Roast until opaque and 63°C at the thickest point, about 10–15 minutes depending on thickness.

Stir @greek yoghurt{150%g}, @dijon mustard{15%g}, @lemon juice{15%ml} and @fresh dill{10%g} together. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve the salmon with the sauce alongside.

title: Red Lentil and Sweet Potato Curry
description: A gently spiced red lentil curry with soft sweet potato and coconut milk.
notes: Add water near the end if the lentils thicken more than desired.
body:
Warm @neutral oil{15%ml} in a saucepan and soften @onion{1}. Add @garlic clove{3}, @fresh ginger{15%g}, @ground cumin{1%tsp}, @ground coriander{1%tsp} and @ground turmeric{0.5%tsp}; stir for 30 seconds. Add @red lentil{250%g}, rinsed, @sweet potato{400%g}, @crushed tomato{400%g}, @coconut milk{400%ml}, @water{300%ml} and @salt{1%tsp}.

Bring to a simmer, cover partially and cook gently, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft and sweet potato is tender, 20–25 minutes. Thin with water if needed. Stir in @lime juice{15%ml} and adjust seasoning.

title: Apple and Oat Crumble
description: Soft cinnamon apples under a crisp topping of oats, flour and butter.
notes: Serve warm. Oven temperatures are suggestions for a home oven.
body:
Heat oven to 190°C conventional (170°C fan). Toss @apple{800%g}, peeled, cored and sliced, with @lemon juice{15%ml}, half of @granulated sugar{40%g} and @ground cinnamon{1%tsp}; spread in a baking dish.

Mix @plain flour{100%g}, @rolled oat{80%g}, @light brown sugar{80%g}, the remaining granulated sugar and @salt{1%pinch}. Rub in @butter{90%g}, cold and diced, until the mixture forms coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces. Scatter evenly over the apples. Bake 35–45 minutes until the fruit bubbles at the edges and the top is golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
